questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Point out incorrect stability order
questions.solution:
Increasing order of stability
(a) $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\right]^{2+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Cu}(\text{ trein })^{2+}\right.$
Their formation of entropy increases in the same order. Ligand denticity is increased.
(b) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\because \quad \mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is weaker ligand than $\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-}$.
$\therefore \quad$ The correct stability order is
$\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)^{3+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}\right.$
(c) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Rh}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\mathrm{Z}_{\text{of }}$ value increases from $\mathrm{Co}^{3+} to \mathrm{Ir}^{3+}$,
(d) $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{1+} \lt  \left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$
O.S of Cr atom increases from $+1 to +3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The total number of possible isomers for squareplanar $\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{Cl})\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)(\mathrm{SCN})\right]^{2-}$ is:
questions.solution: The square planar complex of the type [Mabcd] ^{n \pm}$, where all four ligands are different, has 3 geometrical isomers. But if one of the ligands is ambidentate, then 2 \times 3=6$ geometrical isomers are possible. But if two ligands are ambidentate, then $4 \times 3=12$ geometrical isomers are possible. In the given example, $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$ and $\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$ are ambidentate ligands.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $Amongst \mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4},  \left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}and \left[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-}\right]$
options: $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$ and $\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-}$ are diamagnetic but $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic
$\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic but $\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-}$ is paramagnetic
$\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic but $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$ is paramagnetic
$\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$ is diamagnetic but $\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Ni}$ is

$\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{Ni}(2$8)=[$\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{~d}^{8},$4 $\mathrm{~s}^{2}\\
\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=$[$\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{~d}^{8}$\end{array}Both $\mathrm{Ni}$ and $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ have two unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{CN}^{-}are strong field ligands and thus unpaired electrons get paired. Hence,\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4} and \left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-} are diamagnetic. \mathrm{Cl}^{-}i$s a weak field ligand hence, no pairing of $\mathrme^{-}$will take place. hence $\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}^{2-} is paramagnetic.$

For writing IUPAC name of a co-ordination compound we first write the name of $(+)$ ive complex here. $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{5} \mathrm{Cl}\right]^{2+}$ The names of ligands will come first in alphabatical order, followed by metal ion with its oxidation state written in bracket or parentheis in Roman number i.e. Co (III) here. IUPAC name for cationic complex \rightarrow Pentaamine chloro cobalt (III).
This will follow the name of anion with a gap. i.e. Pentaamine chloro cobalt (III) chloride.

questions.q: The number of unpaired electrons calculated in $\left\{\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right\}^{3+}$ and $\left\{\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{F}_{6}\right)\right\}^{3-}$ are
questions.solution:
In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ and $\left\{\mathrm{CoF}_{6}\right\}^{3-}$ both the oxidation state of cobalt ion $\mathrm{is}+3$. In first case $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is the neutral ligand which is a strong field ligand. hence the electrons in Co (+III) i.e. $4 \mathrm{~s}^{0} 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6}$ get paired to form inner orbital complex. Hence no unpaired electron.
On the other hand $\mathrmF^{-}$is a weak field ligand hence it forms an outer orbital complex with 4 unpaired electrons.
